content.text:
Nature and science facts about sparrows

The sparrow is a small bird, 13–15 cm long, with a chestnut-brown head and a black spot on each cheek. Interestingly, it hops with both feet together and does not walk. Its food changes with the seasons (insects in spring and summer, grain and grass seeds in fall and winter), and it removes parasites with water baths and dust baths. It lays 4–6 eggs at a time and huddles in flocks in winter to keep warm.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why does a sparrow hop instead of walking?
A. It moves by hopping with both feet together. Small birds often do this.

Q. Why do sparrows take dust baths?
A. Along with water baths, it's to remove parasites from between their feathers.

Q. How can we observe sparrows at home?
A. Watch them hop and take dust baths, and talk about how their food changes with the seasons.
